newsitem.title: USA: UAW, Ford announce tentative labor contract.
newsitem.headline: UAW, Ford announce tentative labor contract.

text.p: Ford Motor Co and the United Auto Workers Union said on Monday that they reached a tentative agreement for a new national labor contract.
Ford and UAW officials, at a news conference here, declined to provide details of the pact, but said they expected it to be ratified by September 29.
UAW president Stephen Yokich said the agreement will be presented to the union's Ford council on Wednesday.

The pact, which covers Ford's 105,000 UAW hourly workers, was reached after marathon bargaining sessions over the weekend and Monday. Ford's previous three year contract with the UAW expired at midnight EDT on Saturday.
UAW officials declined to comment on the length of the current pact, but Ford chairman Alex Trotman said earlier on Monday that the two sides had discussed several term lengths beyond three years.
Yokich praised Trotman's direct involvement in the talks. "He's been involved. It used to be you had to go up to see the chairman, now he comes down to see you," Yokich said.

Yokich said he had not decided yet whether or not to target General Motors Corp or Chrysler Corp for the next round of bargaining. He said the decision would be based partly on the outcome of the Canadian talks with Chrysler.
